## Visual Design Reviewer — APPROVE

I compared both running builds in Chromium and inspected the twelve paired disclosure, fixed-panel, surroundings and forced-color sheets. The phone viewport was 390 × 844 and the tablet and desktop viewports were 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900. Each ran in light and pure-black dark mode.

- **Coverage.** I inspected all eleven published panels across Azure documentation, Dynamic Group for Shared Mailboxes, Microsoft Defender SmartScreen, WinGet, Azure Machine Configuration and the Active Directory project article. I hovered and toggled each of the five disclosures and tabbed to and toggled each candidate summary with Space. On Home and the Blog listing I opened Explorer, selected a result with the keyboard in an Azure search and dismissed the overlay. I inspected the neighboring Azure heading and PowerShell fence. I also opened and dismissed the global graph in tablet light and desktop dark on both builds and checked the graph's mobile omission.
- **Changes and hierarchy.** The icon and label retain the common left edge. The chevron now occupies a predictable position at the far end of the row and distinguishes a disclosure from a static note or tip before interaction. Right-facing and downward states read clearly in all three widths. The two PowerShell Version panels agree with each other. The closed Legacy Applications panel reads as one control above Microsoft Intune Rollout. Its keyboard outline encloses the label and chevron. The pointer cursor applies across the summary without reflow on hover.
- **Type and spacing.** Published panels and title rows had the same heights on both builds at every tested width. Candidate summary heights were 58, 60 and 61 CSS pixels. Source Serif 4 title weight 600 and body weight 425 preserve the established hierarchy at 16.175, 17.45 and 18 pixels. Body leading was 26, 28 and 29 pixels. The paragraph and code fence below the Azure panel keep their original measure, and the code continues to use TX-02 at 14.5 pixels.
- **Themes, reflow and motion.** The note retains its quiet blue surface and the tip its green surface, with readable ink against both page colors. The native summary acquires a system interaction color in forced colors. Its arrow and boundary remain distinct. The complete focus mark fits inside the panel at phone width and is visible in dark mode. The five candidate disclosures changed state by mouse and keyboard at every tested width. Reduced-motion disclosure and icon transitions measured zero seconds.
- **Maintainability.** The scoped summary rule uses the existing Quartz icon, palette and reading-line-height token, and the heading adjacency rule recognises the native disclosure. Static panels have no new action marker. The responsive layout needs no separate arrow positioning rule.
- **Defects and severity.** I found no critical, material or minor visual regression. The compact horizontal gap between the focus ring and the tip glyph is visible at full size, and the glyph remains intact. Additional padding there would be a preference.

**Decision — APPROVE.** The trailing chevron and full-row keyboard cue improve recognition while preserving article typography, rhythm and the authored open or closed presentation.

# Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

**Decision — APPROVE.** The five authored disclosures now support keyboard and touch, expose their state and hide collapsed content from assistive technology. I found no material regression.

**Scope.** I opened both previews in Chromium and the candidate in Playwright WebKit at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels in light and pure-black dark themes. I checked all 11 panels on Azure Documentation, Shared Mailboxes, SmartScreen, WinGet, Azure Machine Configuration and the Active Directory project. I inspected the paired disclosures, fixed panels, surroundings and forced-colors sheets across all three widths.

**Navigation and disclosure.** On Shared Mailboxes, Tab reaches the summary. Space closes it and Enter reopens it. Chromium's accessibility tree reported “IMPORTANT” as a disclosure triangle with the matching expanded value each time. Closing removes the Outlook link from the tree and tab sequence, and reopening restores it as the next tab stop. WebKit also skipped the closed body and restored the link. Phone taps opened and closed the same control in both engines. The baseline let readers focus the visually collapsed link. WinGet starts closed. Both PowerShell panels start open. The six ordinary Note and Important panels remain static.

**Readability and reflow.** Source Serif 4 title and body sizes range from 16.175px on phone to 18px on desktop. Summary heights measure 58–61 CSS pixels. Authored line breaks, open-panel geometry, surrounding heading gaps and TX-02 code match the baseline on the pages inspected. WinGet at actual Chromium tab zoom of 200% and 400% reflowed into 640px and 320px layout viewports from a 1280px window. Its open panel, summary, body and inline code fit at both settings without horizontal scrolling.

**Contrast, focus and motion.** Tip-title contrast was 5.24:1 light and 11.57:1 dark. The trailing arrow measured 3.61:1 and 7.60:1 and the body text 16.56:1 and 18.23:1. Chromium's light and dark forced-color palettes kept both icons legible and distinguished the focused summary or authored link with a 2px system-colored outline. Reduced motion yielded zero transition duration on the summary, arrow and body. The summary focus ring stays inside the full-width target.

**Minor inherited defect.** Where the Outlook link wraps to the paragraph's inline-start edge, the callout body's existing overflow rule clips the outer left edge of the focused link's outline on that line. The upper, lower and end edges visibly identify focus. In a matched forced-colors capture at 390px, every body pixel including the link outline matched the baseline. Severity is minor and pre-existing. I recorded no discretionary design change.

**Surroundings and maintenance.** I exercised Home search, Arrow Down and Escape, mobile Explorer, Blog listing to Azure article via SPA, and adjacent code. Global Graph opened a canvas at 900 and 1440 and Escape returned focus on both builds. It was hidden on phone and under reduced motion. The disclosure transformer uses native HTML state and leaves the named source text and links in place. The narrow CSS rules reuse the existing type, theme and focus styles.

**Independent evidence.** Browser measurements are in access-chromium.json and access-webkit.json. Native zoom and site-navigation results are in access-zoom-ui.json. The separate network-enabled graph run is in access-graph.json. Focus captures are in access-images, including author-focus-47832.png and author-focus-47833.png. The accessibility tree was inspected with browser tooling. A physical screen reader was outside this review's coverage.

# CSS and Quartz V5 review

**REVISE.** A real search-result selection loses the reader's place on an article with a foldable callout.

## Demonstrated defect

**Material — search result navigation.** In Chromium at 900 × 900, start at the Blog archive, search for `Legacy Applications`, and select *Automatically Update Apps through Intune (WinGet)*. Baseline 47832 highlights the title and scrolls to the collapsed panel, with the panel approximately 430px from the viewport top. Candidate 47833 stays at scroll position 0. The panel is 1767px below the viewport top and its title gets no highlight. The installed Search resource includes paragraphs and blockquotes in its body-text selector, so it no longer sees the title after its conversion to summary/span.

Repeat with the body-only query `employee requires older version`. Both builds insert a search highlight. Baseline scrolls to the collapsed panel, with its top at 399px. Candidate leaves the disclosure closed and stays at scroll position 0. A selected result should bring the matched title into view and make a match inside the body visible. The authored default and normal keyboard activation should still work on ordinary visits. [Baseline search screenshot](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-finding-title-47832.png) · [Candidate search screenshot](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-finding-title-47833.png) · [Title reproduction](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-search.cjs) · [Body reproduction](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-search-body.cjs)

## Independent inspection

- Opened the baseline and candidate in Chromium at 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900 in the warm-light and pure-black themes. Compared all 12 paired sheets for disclosures, fixed callouts, forced colors and their article surroundings. Exercised Home, the Blog archive, Explorer controls, search results, Azure Machine Configuration's callout and adjacent PowerShell code, WinGet's default-closed callout, Azure documentation's fixed note and navigation between articles. The archive showed 176 entries on both builds. Ordinary PowerShell search returned eight results on both. Home shows the graph at 900 and 1440 and omits it at 390. Verified the global graph opens to a canvas and Escape returns focus at 1440. [Browser matrix](/tmp/quartz-callout-pass/css-matrix.json)
- The Azure callout retained its 354.9, 656.5 and 688px widths and its 58, 60 and 61px summary heights, respectively. Theme title inks agreed at each width. Title/prose use Source Serif 4, Explorer uses SN Pro, and technical code uses TX-02. Column and heading alignment, fixed callouts and body wrapping agree across the pairs. The arrow moves to the inline end. Keyboard focus produces a solid inset outline across the summary. Forced-color icons use black and white system ink in the light and dark scenarios. No horizontal overflow appeared.
- Native Enter opens and Space closes the disclosure in all candidate cells. Three consecutive Quartz render events preserve state, then one click toggles once. The checkbox-free native structure also supplies the keyboard stop absent in the baseline. The transformer removes the two state classes that the OFM resource uses for activation. Native details owns the state independently of the V5 nav/render listeners.
- Read the installed OFM generator and click handler, the installed Search jump selector, the transform, its registration after configured HTML transformers, and the new tests and SCSS. The direct children match the actual OFM title/icon/body structure. The HAST pass retains links, emphasis, metadata, body content and the order of nested disclosures. It strips the inactive arrow when there is no meaningful body and skips static notes. The focused tests passed 2/2 independently. No new dependency or client-side event handler was introduced in the submitted cycle. Details-specific styling preserves upstream mask, color and reduced-motion rules, with direct-child selectors isolating nested controls.

The search behavior above is the only material issue identified in this cycle.

# Design Director review — first callout candidate

**REVISE.** The Visual Design and Responsive and Accessibility reviewers approved the native disclosure. The CSS and Quartz V5 reviewer identified a material regression in Search navigation. I reproduced it independently on both live builds. The two approvals establish that the panels themselves are ready. The Search regression blocks acceptance of this candidate.

In Chrome at 900 × 900, selecting WinGet from Blog Search for **Legacy Applications** on the baseline scrolled the matched title into the viewport and highlighted it. On the candidate the page stayed at the top, the panel began 1,767px below the top and the title had no match marker. Searching for **employee requires older version** created a marker inside the closed candidate disclosure and left the reader at the top. Restore Search's jump to the title while keeping its authored closed state. For a body match, reveal its owning disclosure before scrolling to the match. [Title comparison](director-search-47833-Legacy.json) · [Body comparison](director-search-47833-employee.json)

My live Shared Mailboxes checks at 390, 900 and 1440px confirmed that closing the candidate removes the Outlook link from keyboard focus and the browser accessibility tree. Space reopens the summary and Tab then reaches the link. With page scripts disabled, both pointer and keyboard still toggle the native disclosure. Phone and desktop dark-mode checks resolved to a black page when the site theme was active. The published screenshots show a clear trailing chevron and a distinct focus mark across the title row. The minor clipping of an outer focus edge on a wrapped body link appears on both builds. It does not account for the Search regression. [Director browser observations](director-browser.json) · [Mobile detail](director-mobile.png)

The build emitted 913 files and all 166 unit tests passed. The separate repository-wide type check still reports the two inherited dependency declaration errors. I inspected the full visual, responsive/accessibility and CSS/Quartz assessments, the paired evidence and the transformer and scoped styles. Recheck the two Search selections, the ordinary authored open/closed states and the surrounding navigation on the corrected production build before acceptance.
